items.question: Do the researchers discuss limitations, threats to validity, assumptions, or scope boundaries?

quality_checklist.overall_rationale: The paper is credible and strong on conceptual traceability of technical measures in a CubeSat SysML reference model. Its limitations are lack of EPS-specific modeling, absent empirical outcome evidence, limited toolchain/reproducibility detail, and only future-work treatment of verification/validation artifacts.

RQ1.rationale: The study offers a general CubeSat reference-model pattern for technical measures and qualitative-to-quantitative modeling, but it is not an EPS model and does not claim minimal behavioral knowledge as a primary objective.

RQ2.rationale: It claims system-level benefits such as traceability, trade analysis, generalizability, reduced risk, and possible CubeSat success improvement; EPS-specific reliability, reproducibility, and integrability outcomes are not reported.

RQ3.rationale: Technical measures are tied conceptually to verification and validation and can be analyzed before implementation, but the paper states that V&V model elements remain future work and provides no EPS verification procedure.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper is part of the INCOSE Space Systems Working Group CubeSat Reference Model lineage and cites an interim status paper, but no prior extraction or related paper was consulted for this extraction.

RQ1: The paper proposes a general SysML pattern for CubeSat technical measures: stakeholder concerns -> mission objectives -> MOE specifications/value properties -> MOPs -> TPMs.
Limited early behavioral knowledge is handled indirectly through qualitative MOE/MOP/TPM specification elements, but quantitative analysis still requires empirical or analytical relationships.
The study is not EPS-specific; battery cycles and solar cell life are only power-adjacent MOP examples for service life.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include traceability, qualitative-measure capture, trade analysis, generalizability, and possible mission-success/risk benefits.
No EPS-specific reliability, reproducibility, or integrability outcome is demonstrated.
Evidence is mainly diagrams and author reasoning, without metrics, comparison, integration/test evidence, or flight data.
RQ3: Technical measures are positioned as a basis for validation and verification: MOEs validate user needs, MOPs verify requirements, and TPMs monitor technical requirements.
Parametric diagrams can support pre-physical assessment of whether lower-level measures satisfy higher-level objectives.
The authors state that actual V&V model elements remain future work, so verification procedures are not fully integrated, and no EPS verification procedure is reported.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: Future work is needed to incorporate model elements associated with those activities and relate them to the technical measures discussed here.
However, this approach is not complete and provides no traceability to stakeholder expectations, connections between technical measures, and connections with requirements.

Verification and validation are discussed conceptually, while V&V model elements are deferred to future work.
